title: Legacy Forum Content Governance
business: A community-driven historical archive platform hosting millions of legacy text posts.
problem: The platform struggles with high volumes of user-generated content that may violate community safety guidelines, requiring a consistent, cost-effective way to flag potentially harmful text without migrating to newer, more complex model architectures.
solution: By integrating the text-moderation-stable model, the platform can programmatically scan incoming and existing text submissions against safety categories. This model provides a stable, locked-in snapshot (text-moderation-007) that ensures consistent classification behavior for legacy datasets, avoiding the variability that might arise from frequent model updates.
steps: Identify the specific text fields in the legacy database requiring moderation.
Configure the application to route text payloads to the v1/moderations endpoint.
Utilize the text-moderation-007 snapshot to ensure consistent classification logic.
Implement a conditional logic gate to flag or block content based on the model's returned categories.
Log the moderation results for audit trails and manual review queues.
outcome: The platform achieves a predictable and automated safety filtering process that maintains historical consistency across its archive.
limitation: The primary limitation is that text-moderation-stable is a text-only model and cannot process multimodal content like images or audio. To check for this, developers must validate input types before calling the moderation endpoint; if the input contains non-text media, the system should trigger a fallback error handler.
